title: The square that came back
text: The QR code was invented {{1}} Japan in 1994 {{2}} track car parts moving along a production line, and for twenty years it sat quietly in the background of logistics. {{3}} was not until billions of people carried camera-equipped phones {{4}} the humble square found its true audience, and the pandemic then made scanning a reflex: menus opened {{5}} a wave of the phone, and businesses {{6}} websites had lagged for years suddenly had a doorway in every poster. The square even appears {{7}} gravestones, {{8}} a scan calls up photographs and a life story for anyone standing in the churchyard with a signal.

gaps.explanation: 'Invented to track' — the infinitive of purpose.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ was not until phones spread
gaps.explanation: 'It was not until X that…' — the fixed cleft frame.

gaps.hint: conjunction: not until phones ___ the square found
gaps.explanation: The second half of the 'not until' cleft: that.

gaps.hint: preposition: opened ___ a wave of the phone
gaps.explanation: 'With a wave' — the means of opening.
'Whose' links the businesses to their websites.

gaps.hint: relative adverb: gravestones, ___ a scan calls up
gaps.explanation: 'Where' refers back to the gravestones as the place.
